facts.fact: Requests officially supports Python 3.10 and newer.
Requests no longer supports Python 2.7; support was dropped in Requests 2.28.0.
facts.source_quote: No! As of Requests 2.28.0, Requests no longer supports Python 2.7.

facts.fact: The documented way to install Requests is `python -m pip install requests` (not pipenv or easy_install).
The Requests source repository lives at github.com/psf/requests.
chardet is not a mandatory dependency; unless chardet is already installed or the [use_chardet_on_py3] extra is used, Requests uses charset-normalizer to guess response encodings.
facts.source_quote: and ``chardet`` is not already installed, ``requests`` uses ``charset-normalizer``

docs.expected_stale: yes: 'Requests officially supports Python 2.7 & 3.4–3.7, and runs great on PyPy.' (contradicts F1, F2); also '$ pipenv install requests' / 'simply use pipenv (or pip, of course)' (F3) and 'Fork the repository (https://github.com/requests/requests) on GitHub' (F4)
yes: 'Yes! Requests officially supports Python 2.7 & 3.5+ and PyPy.' (F1, F2); also 'We do not have immediate plans to sunset our support for Python 2.7.' (F2)

docs.inserted: If the headers do not declare a charset, Requests falls back to the ``chardet`` library, which is always installed alongside Requests as a required dependency.
Requests currently supports Python 3.8 and newer, so your change should pass the test suite on each of those versions before you open a Pull Request.
Requests 2.27.1, released in January 2022, was the last release to support Python 2.7.
Before version 2.26.0, released in July 2021, ``chardet`` was a mandatory dependency of Requests on every Python version.
